quality_info.title: Quality — how the 0–100 score is built
quality_info.summary: A 0–100 read of how the last filed quarters' earnings were built: growth backed by sales, margins widening, growth rates speeding up — minus penalties for a beat with no sales behind it and for inventory piling up.
quality_info.measured_note: A description of the company's last filed quarters, not a measured predictor of returns: no study on this app has tested whether a higher Quality score leads to better forward returns.
quality_info.weights_note: The point weights and most cut-offs are this app's own choices.

points.label: EPS growth
points.rule: Latest quarter's EPS vs the same quarter a year ago: 0 points at 0% or below, rising evenly to the full 20 at +25% or more.

points.label: Sales score
points.rule: The app's Sales score (0–100) scaled down to 20. It rises with sales growth vs a year ago, with bonuses — only at +5% growth or more — for accelerating sales, consecutive growing quarters and sales outgrowing EPS.

points.label: Net margin vs a year ago
points.rule: Latest quarter's net margin vs the same quarter a year ago: 15 if it widened by more than 0.5 percentage point, 0 if it narrowed by more than that, 7 if in between or unknown.

points.label: EPS growth speeding up
points.rule: 12 if the EPS growth rate rose step by step across the last three quarters (oldest lowest, latest highest and above zero); 6 if only the latest quarter's rate beat the one before (and is above zero); otherwise 0.

points.label: Sales growth speeding up
points.rule: 12 if the sales growth rate rose step by step across the last three quarters (latest above zero); 6 if the Sales score calls sales accelerating (latest quarter's growth above the one before, and above zero); otherwise 0.

points.label: Net margin rising
points.rule: 11 if net margin rose step by step across the last three quarters, quarter over quarter; otherwise 0.

points.label: Earnings surprise
points.rule: Up to 10: the earnings surprise in %, capped. This app's data path never passes a surprise in, so it is 0 on every name today.

penalties.label: A beat with no sales behind it
penalties.rule: EPS up 25% or more on sales up less than 5%, with net margin not widening by more than 0.5 point year over year.

penalties.label: Double trouble
penalties.rule: The ⚠️ flag AND receivables growing more than 15 points faster than sales (and above 10%): takes 20 instead of the 10. Receivables are read only for the names that get the supplemental read.

quality_info.ceiling_note: Added up and clamped to 0–100, then rounded. The most a name can score today is 90: the surprise points never arrive.

tiers.label: 🎯 Code 33
tiers.rule: EPS growth rate, sales growth rate and net margin all rose step by step across the last three quarters (EPS and sales growth above zero in the latest).

tiers.label: Red flag
tiers.rule: Double trouble, a beat with no sales behind it, or the ⚠️ inventory flag.

tiers.label: Accelerating
tiers.rule: The latest EPS growth rate beat the quarter before (and is above zero), or sales are accelerating — and net margin did not narrow by more than 0.5 point year over year.

tiers.label: Steady
tiers.rule: None of the above, and a score of 55 or more.

tiers.label: Weak
tiers.rule: Everything else that has a score.

tiers.label: Blank (—)
tiers.rule: No score: neither EPS nor sales can be compared with a year ago for the latest quarter — fewer than 5 quarters on file, the latest or the year-ago quarter missing, or a year-ago value of zero.

quality_info.tier_note: The first tier that matches wins, in this order. Hover a score to see its tier.

marks.rule: Inventory grew more than 15 points faster than sales year over year, inventory growth is above 10%, and sales growth is below 25% (a build alongside strong sales is left alone). Total inventory only.

blank: Neither EPS nor sales can be compared with a year ago for the latest quarter — fewer than 5 quarters on file, the latest or the year-ago quarter missing, or a year-ago value of zero.
Names whose fundamentals came from the fallback data source are left unscored on purpose — the score is only computed from the filing-backed data.
The name's research-cache row is older than 16 days, so the board does not use it.
No research-cache row for the name yet.
quality_info.group_rows: Sector, industry and roster rows show the median score of their full membership, with no 🎯 or ⚠️.

fundamentals_as_of.note: From the research cache, which a scheduled job refreshes — a fresh print shows here only after its next run. A row older than 16 days is not used.

amd.title: IMO: AMD marked up · 32d ago. 🌀 AMD is the app's manipulation read: the module's own cycle phase — a base was built, its low was swept and price CLOSED back inside (raided), or the markup happened (marked up), or the base gave way (base failed). IT IS MEASURED INVERTED ON ITS OWN CLAIM. Re-measured 2026-09-14 on 3,712 names / 1,592,057 bars: Fires on 15.1% of bars. Forward returns are negative at every horizon (5d −0.36% [−0.77, −0.06], 10d −0.48% [−1.07, −0.02], 21d −0.41% [−1.11, +0.15]). Like-for-like against a bar inside its OWN live base at the same distance below the top it reaches the base top LESS often — 51.9% vs 56.1%, −4.2pp [−6.92, −1.89], negative in all seven distance buckets. The board's own freshest cut is worse still: The board's own 0-3 cut is worse: −5.6pp [−8.97, −2.69]. So this is a STATE, not a ranking and not a quality score: a fresh raid is not a reason to buy, and this app measured it going the other way. It sorts nothing, filters nothing, orders nothing, colours nothing and gates nothing. Re-runnable: backend/scripts/turning_bullish_amd_study.py; written up in docs/supply_demand/turning_bullish.md.
